title: Fork-lift truck
prompt: A labelled static scale teaching adaptation of the page 56 fork-lift counterweight example carries a specimen on forks fixed at a chosen height. Add load places a heavier specimen on the fixed forks. Compare counterweight externally exchanges two rear ballast specimens. Show moments overlays the opposing gravitational moments about the front-wheel contact line and indicates when the rear wheels would lose contact. See-through shows the chassis, front and rear wheels, mast, fixed forks, load and rear counterweight. The ballast exchange and fixed fork height are teaching fixtures, not operating truck controls. Do not animate lift, tilt or driving, or add hydraulic and chain internals absent from this source.
chapter: Part 1: The Mechanics of Movement / Pulleys
blurb: A fixed-fork teaching adaptation shows how rear ballast opposes a front load and prevents forward toppling.
adaptation: Declared static scale counterweight and longitudinal stability teaching adaptation, not an operating forklift reconstruction.
truthNotes: Fixed forks and external specimen exchanges are teaching fixtures, not operating controls.
Animations highlight substituted specimens and fade moment overlays; no lifting, tilting or driving.
Force arrows, moment arcs, contact markers and load specimen do not count as anatomy.
Illustrative scale masses and lumped truck centre are not truck ratings. Truck self-weight is included in the restoring moment.
An upright static diagram reports when rear contact would be lost without simulating a fall.
Hydraulic, chain, lift and tilt internals are omitted because the inspected source does not establish them.
Saved 1998 and 2016 printed pages 56 and 57 support the named counterweight principle. 1988 is inaccessible and unverified. No edition-union claim.
